switch.title: Add a water heater
switch.description: Choose the switch that turns the heater on and the sensor that measures the water.

data_description.temperature_sensor: A sensor measuring the stored water's temperature.
data_description.power_sensor: With a power sensor, a heater that draws nothing and a relay stuck on are noticed too.

climate.title: Add a water heater with a thermostat
climate.description: Choose the thermostat that runs the heater and the sensor that measures the water. Hot Water Ready sets its mode and setpoint.

data_description.name: Shown on the card and on the heater's device, for example Cylinder.
data_description.temperature_sensor: A sensor measuring the stored water's temperature.
data_description.power_sensor: With a power sensor, a heater that draws power while the thermostat is off is noticed, and, if the thermostat says when it heats, one that draws nothing.
data_description.climate: Hot Water Ready sets it to heat at the stop temperature, or off.

reconfigure.title: Change the water heater
reconfigure.description: How Home Assistant turns the heating element on.

abort.already_configured: This switch already belongs to a heater.

error.unsupported_thermostat: This thermostat cannot be set to heat and off; choose another, or a switch.

user.title: Add a member
user.description: A linked member is a person who sets their own times and is told when the water is ready. A virtual member, such as Global or Guests, has no person; an administrator sets its times.

data_description.notify_targets: Leave empty to find this person's phones automatically.

data_description.recipients: People told when this member's water is ready. Leave empty to tell nobody.

data_description.notify_targets: Leave empty to find this person's phones automatically.

options.lower_third: About a third of the way up

data.keep_heating_gap_minutes: Keep heating through gaps shorter than
data.keep_hot_minutes: After heat now, keep the water hot for
data.max_temperature: Highest temperature for showers close together
data.cancel_people: People who may switch off the heating for everyone

data_description.keep_heating_gap_minutes: Ready times this close share one window and the heater keeps heating through, instead of letting the water cool in between.
data_description.keep_hot_minutes: Counted from the "hot water ready" message; meanwhile the water is kept between the target minus and plus the margin. 0: stop at the message. Holding the card's button picks another time for that request, up to 120 minutes.
data_description.cancel_people: Besides the administrators. Whoever asked may always cancel their own request.
data_description.rich_notifications: On phones with the Home Assistant app, "Hot water ready" replaces "heating" instead of arriving as a second message.
data_description.power_sensor: With a power sensor, a heater that draws nothing and a relay stuck on are noticed too.
data_description.solar_aware: Off: the start is worked out from the heater alone, and the solar-aware result is only recorded, for the comparison in the card's settings.
data_description.heating_rate: Minutes to raise the water one degree. Empty: learned from the heater's own runs.
data_description.tank_litres: With the element power, lets the heater heat higher for showers close together that the tank at the normal target cannot carry.
data_description.element_watts: Also gives the solar comparison its kWh without a power sensor.
data_description.max_temperature: 50 °C is the scald limit without a mixing valve; up to 60 °C only with one.
data_description.element_height: Heat rises, so the water below the element barely warms. With the volume and power, this gives the range the heating speed should fall in.
data_description.middle_temperature_sensor: A probe in the middle of the tank. The start comes forward when the water below the top is colder, and both probes are checked against how they normally behave. Ready still follows the main probe.
data_description.top_probe_height: Where the main probe sits, from the bottom (0%) to the top (100%) of the tank.
data_description.middle_probe_height: With both heights, each probe counts for the heated water nearest it, so the mean the start is worked out from is weighted. Without them, half each.

sensor_unavailable.title: {heater}: the water temperature sensor is silent
sensor_unavailable.description: No reading from the water temperature sensor for a while, so heating is stopped. It starts again by itself a minute after readings come back.

not_rising.title: {heater}: the water is not getting hotter

confirm.title: Is it fixed?
confirm.description: The heater was on for a long time and the water barely rose, so heating is stopped. Check the heater and its breaker, then confirm here that it is fixed. Confirm that the heater has been checked and fixed. Heating starts again.

confirm.title: Is it fixed?
confirm.description: The relay was on but the heater drew almost no power, so heating is stopped. Check the element and its breaker, then confirm here that it is fixed. Confirm that the heater has been checked and fixed. Heating starts again.

relay_stuck.title: {heater}: the heater draws power while switched off
relay_stuck.description: The heater is drawing power although the relay is off. The relay may be stuck on; check it. This clears by itself a minute after the power stops.

top_probe.title: {heater}: the main probe may be loose

confirm.title: Is it fixed?
confirm.description: The main water probe rose more slowly than it normally does on two heats running. It may be coming out of its pocket or exposed to the cold. Check it, then confirm here; it also clears by itself after a normal heat.

middle_probe.title: {heater}: the second probe may be loose

confirm.title: Is it fixed?
confirm.description: The second probe rose more slowly than it normally does, or fell behind the main one, on two heats running. Until it reads properly again the start is worked out from the main probe alone. Check it, then confirm here.

confirm.title: Is it fixed?
confirm.description: For half an hour the main probe read more than 3 °C colder than the second one. Hot water rises, so one of them is not reading the water. Check both, then confirm here.

heat_now.name: Heat now
heat_now.description: Heats the water now. The member named is told when it is ready; without one, the person who asked, if any.

member.name: Member
member.description: Who to tell when it is ready.

keep_minutes.name: Keep hot for
keep_minutes.description: Minutes to keep the water hot after the message. Empty: the heater's setting.

add_ready_time.name: Add a ready time
add_ready_time.description: Adds a time when a member wants hot water.

time.name: Time
time.description: When the water should be ready.

weekdays.name: Days
weekdays.description: The days it repeats on. Left out: every day.

enabled.name: On
enabled.description: Off keeps the time without acting on it.

remove_ready_time.name: Remove a ready time
remove_ready_time.description: Removes a member's ready times at a time of day, whatever their days.

set_away.name: Set away
set_away.description: Pauses or resumes a member's ready times.

away.name: Away
away.description: On pauses the ready times, off resumes them.

until.name: Until
until.description: The last day away; after it, away ends by itself.

switch_off.name: Switch off
switch_off.description: Switches the heater off now for everyone: the heat-now request ends and the ready times it was heating for are skipped. Everyone who loses out is told.
